calls.title: Google Analytics Project - Timothy
calls.summary: The team plans to shift from gtag to Google Tag Manager to enhance event tracking on their new Webflow website, enabling better management of tags for various platforms like Google Analytics and HubSpot. Key tracking goals include understanding user journeys, form submissions, and conversion funnels to guide content strategies. Custom event listeners will be incorporated to capture conversions from forms without thank you pages. The setup is estimated to take 3 to 4 days, with data collection beginning after 24 hours of activation. The Ad Specialist emphasized the importance of integrating paid ads with robust tracking to optimize performance, while also balancing paid traffic with organic growth strategies.
calls.keywords: Google Tag Manager, GA4, Webflow, HubSpot forms, tracking events, digital ads

calls.title: Google Analytics Project - Jordi
calls.summary: The team discussed the implementation of Google Analytics 4 (GA4) and Google Tag Manager (GTM) to enhance event tracking on their new Webflow-built website. They prioritized the integration of GA4 and GTM for monitoring custom events, moving beyond standard page views to capture specific user interactions like button clicks. Jordi emphasized validating Webflow's compatibility with GTM for effective event tracking. The initial implementation plan spans about 40 hours over two weeks, rolling out event tracking incrementally for data accuracy. They prefer using BigQuery for its easier integration with other marketing tools and decided to utilize Notion for task tracking and team collaboration. Immediate next steps include reviewing the Webflow setup and planning a follow-up meeting for alignment on project scope.
calls.keywords: GA4, Google Tag Manager, Webflow, BigQuery, Clickhouse, Event Tracking
